title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page does not belong to the divided-power de Rham notes around it. It is a typed page, numbered '- 62 -' with the running head 'IX', from Grothendieck's Exposé IX of SGA 7 I, 'Modèles de Néron et monodromie'. It most likely survives because Grothendieck reused typescript sheets as scrap paper; the neighbouring pages are handwritten computations about the divided-power (pd) algebra A_1 = S{X_0,X_1,dX_0,dX_1}/(X_0+X_1−T, dX_0+dX_1)_pd.

Setting.
- S is a henselian (here complete) trait with generic point η and fraction field K.
- A_K is an abelian variety over K with semi-stable reduction. A_K' is its dual, A^o and A'^o are the identity components of their Néron models, and T_o and T'_o are the toric parts of their special fibres.
- For every prime ℓ, including ℓ = p (the residue characteristic), the Tate module T_ℓ(A_K) is viewed as a pro-ℓ Barsotti–Tate group (an inverse system of finite flat group schemes).
- It carries the monodromy filtration T^t ⊂ T^f ⊂ T. Here T^f is the 'fixed' or finite part, coming from the Néron model, and T^t is the toric part.

Proposition 5.6. Assume S is complete and A_K has semi-stable reduction. Then:
1. T^t is the generic fibre of a pro-BT group over S of toric type, given by (5.5.7). Concretely it is Hom of the twisted constant character group into Z_ℓ(1), i.e. the Tate module of the torus lifting T_o.
2. T/T^f is the generic fibre of a pro-étale pro-BT group over S, given by (5.5.8); it is the twisted constant group attached to M'.
3. T^f extends to S as T_ℓ(A^o)^f.
4. T/T^t extends to S as D(T_ℓ(A'^o)^f) = Hom(T_ℓ(A'^o)^f, Z_ℓ(1)), the Cartier/Serre dual in the pro-BT sense.

Point 4 is a reformulation of the orthogonality theorem (T^t is the orthogonal of T'^f under the Weil pairing), lifted to group schemes over S. This matters when ℓ = p, where Galois modules alone do not capture the structure.

5.6.1. An étale cover S' splits T^t if and only if it splits T/T^f. These conditions mean S' splits the twisted constant groups M and M' respectively, and M and M' are isogenous because the tori T_o and T'_o are. Hence a smallest étale extension S' doing the job exists, namely the splitting field of the torus. The page ends by announcing a corollary of the definitions in 2.2.3.

The mathematics serves the study of monodromy and Galois/flat structure of Tate modules under semi-stable reduction, uniformly in ℓ including ℓ = p.
errors: No mathematical errors visible; the statement is consistent with the orthogonality theorem of SGA 7 IX (T^t = orthogonal of T'^f), which gives T/T^t ≅ dual of T'^f.
Contextual note: the page is unrelated to the handwritten pd–de Rham computations on the neighbouring pages; it is a recycled typescript sheet.

ideas.what: Extension of the toric part, fixed part and quotients of T_ℓ(A_K), including ℓ = p, to pro-Barsotti–Tate groups over S (toric type, pro-étale type, Néron-model part, dual of the dual's fixed part)
ideas.modern_name: Filtration of the p-divisible group of a semi-stable abelian variety (toric / abelian / étale parts); Raynaud–Grothendieck uniformization at the level of BT groups
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck, SGA 7 I, Exp. IX (1967–69, publ. 1972)

ideas.what: Duality D = Hom(−, Z_ℓ(1)) for pro-BT groups expressing T/T^t as the dual of T'^f
ideas.modern_name: Cartier/Serre duality of p-divisible groups plus the orthogonality theorem

ideas.what: A minimal étale extension splits both T^t and T/T^f, because the twisted character groups M and M' are isogenous
ideas.modern_name: Splitting field of the toric part of the Néron model

deep.surprise_reason: This is a typed page of the published SGA 7 Exposé IX (Prop. 5.6), probably reused as scrap paper inside the pd–de Rham notes. Its content is well known and credited to Grothendieck; the only curiosity is archival, namely its physical presence in this folder.
transcription_corrections: Transcription is essentially accurate. 'Ainsi' is typed as shown (slightly smudged in the image). The archive stamp '380' and the handwritten '190' are folio numbers, not mathematical content.
